chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali al-Sa'i, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, I used to practice Mut'ah (temporary marriage), but I disliked it and took it as an ill omen, so I made a covenant with Allah between the Rukn and the Maqam, and I made upon myself a vow and fasting that I would not practice it. Then indeed that became difficult for me, and I repented of my oath, but I have the strength in my hand to practice it openly.' He said to me: 'You made a covenant with Allah that you would obey Him, and by Allah, if you do not obey Him, you will disobey Him.'

key_terms.الرُّكْن وَالْمَقَام: The Rukn and Maqam (specific corners of the Kaaba where covenants are made)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on breaking a vow made to Allah regarding temporary marriage (Mut'ah)?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Isfahani, the companion’s vow to abstain from Mut'ah is treated as a covenant with Allah, where the Imam emphasizes that fulfilling the vow is an act of obedience, while breaking it is disobedience. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that vows regarding permissible acts carry binding weight, and the Imam’s response underscores the spiritual gravity of keeping one's word to God. The context reflects the practical application of vow-breaking (kaffarah) within the framework of personal piety and divine covenant.
